Elaine: quick sanity check — porting a tiny sample to the new Go SDK and getting 401s only from the client. curl with the same key works. Key was copied out of 1Password. anyone seen invisible chars that curl tolerates but net/http doesn't?

Raj: yup. 1Password can add a trailing newline or an odd control char. curl often sends what you give it, or people accidentally use quotes. first try: print the bytes to inspect: 

Elaine: oof that helped. what exact command do you recommend?

Raj: run either of these on the file/env var to check for weird bytes:

```
# if you have the key in $API_KEY
printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | hexdump -C
# or if the key is in a file
xxd -g 1 api_key.txt
```

Raj: common culprits: CR (0d), UTF-8 BOM (ef bb bf), or an accidental trailing space. Also if you base64-encode manually, make sure to disable line wrapping.

Nate: small tip specific to basic auth: the service expects Basic <base64(api_key:)> (API key as username, empty password). If you set the header manually, do: 

```
# POSIX shell
auth=$(printf '%s:' "$API_KEY" | base64 --wrap=0)
curl -H "Authorization: Basic $auth" https://api.redwood.example/generate
```

Mira: for Go, don't craft the header yourself — let the stdlib do it so you avoid encoding mistakes: 

```
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, body)
req.SetBasicAuth(apiKey, "")
```

Mira: SetBasicAuth will automatically append the colon and base64-encode; it also avoids accidental CR/LF if you read from a file with ReadString.

Elaine: interesting — I was doing `Authorization: Basic {{base64 .Env.API_KEY}}` in a template and I think I forgot the colon.

Raj: that would explain curl working if you manually typed the header and the client failing if the colon was missing. Also check for any proxy or ingress that strips or lowercases headers — some setups normalize header names which can bite custom middleware.

Nate: another gotcha: if you're mounting the key via Docker secret and reading with `cat /run/secrets/key`, many editors/tools add a newline at EOF. Use `tr -d '\r\n'` when loading into env in bash, or `strings.TrimSpace` in Go.

Elaine: tried `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | hexdump -C` — showed a \r at the end. ran `API_KEY=$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | tr -d '\r\n')` and client works now. thanks!! :tada:

Mira: PR idea: update the Go SDK sample to use `req.SetBasicAuth(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"), "")` and add a note about trimming and common control chars. small change, big help.

Elaine: I'll open the PR this afternoon and add the hexdump troubleshooting snippet. cc @ci-bot for tests.

ci-bot: build queued — will run SDK samples lint and unit tests when PR is up.

Raj: also add a one-liner for Windows PowerShell users (they often paste with CRLF): `($env:REDWOOD_API_KEY).Trim()` in PS.

Elaine: good call. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
